import { Backpack, Blocks, Braces, CheckCircle2, FileCode, FlaskConical, ReceiptText, Search, ShieldCheck, Terminal, TriangleAlert } from 'lucide-react';

Deploy an existing Anchor workspace to Gorbagana. You'll configure `Anchor.toml`, align the Program ID, build the workspace, deploy or upgrade the program, and verify the result in the explorer.

<Callout type="info" title="Gorbagana-specific Anchor docs">
  This page covers Gorbagana RPC, native GOR funding, deployment verification, and explorer links. Use the [official Anchor docs](https://www.anchor-lang.com/docs) for framework syntax, account constraints, tests, CLI flags, and general client APIs.
</Callout>

Before a live deploy, run the [Testing](/build/testing) flow and review the [Security checklist](/build/security-checklist).

## Command reference

Use these commands for the common Anchor deployment flow.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Check Anchor version | `anchor --version` |
| List workspace program IDs | `anchor keys list` |
| Sync `declare_id!` with program keypairs | `anchor keys sync` |
| Build programs and IDLs | `anchor build` |
| Deploy workspace programs | `anchor deploy` |
| Upgrade one program | `anchor upgrade <target/deploy/program.so> --program-id <PROGRAM_ID>` |
| Fetch published IDL | `anchor idl fetch -o <out-file.json> <PROGRAM_ID>` |
| Show deployed program metadata | `solana program show <PROGRAM_ID>` |

## What you need

Prepare the workspace before you deploy.

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| RPC endpoint | `https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf` |
| Wallet | A local keypair funded with native GOR |
| Tooling | Solana CLI, Rust, and Anchor CLI |
| Program ID | The address declared in `declare_id!` and used by clients |
| Explorer | `https://explorer.gorbagana.wtf` |

<Callout type="info" title="Anchor wraps the same loader model">
  Anchor deploys SVM programs through the same upgradeable loader used by `solana program deploy`. Use [Deploy programs](/build/deploy-programs) when you need lower-level authority, close, or bytecode-management details.
</Callout>

## Configure Anchor.toml

Point Anchor at Gorbagana with the provider URL and the wallet that pays deployment costs.

```toml
[provider]
cluster = "https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf"
wallet = "~/.config/solana/id.json"
```

If your frontend needs generated TypeScript IDL types, copy them into a stable folder during builds.

```toml
[workspace]
types = "app/src/idl/"
```

Anchor's official `Anchor.toml` reference defines `[provider]` as the wallet and cluster used by Anchor commands. For Gorbagana, use the RPC URL directly as the cluster value.

## Align the program ID

Anchor programs need one Program ID across the Rust program, generated keypair, workspace config, and clients.

<Steps>
<Step>

### List workspace keys

Run this from the Anchor workspace root.

```bash
anchor keys list
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Check the generated program keypair

Print the Program ID from the generated keypair.

```bash
solana address -k ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana-keypair.json
```

Replace `hello_gorbagana` with your Anchor program name.

</Step>
<Step>

### Check declare_id!

Open the program entrypoint and confirm `declare_id!` matches the keypair address.

```rust
use anchor_lang::prelude::*;

declare_id!("PROGRAM_ID");
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Sync keys when they differ

If the generated keypair and `declare_id!` don't match, sync the workspace.

```bash
anchor keys sync
```

Review the file changes after syncing. Then rebuild before deploying.

</Step>
</Steps>

If your workspace keeps a `[programs.<cluster>]` section, set that program entry to the same Program ID. The important rule is simple: clients, `declare_id!`, and deployment keypairs must point to the same address.

## Build the workspace

Build the Anchor workspace after you configure the provider and align program IDs.

```bash
anchor build
```

Anchor writes deployment and client artifacts under `target`.

```txt
target/
  deploy/
    hello_gorbagana.so
    hello_gorbagana-keypair.json
  idl/
    hello_gorbagana.json
  types/
    hello_gorbagana.ts
```

The `.so` file is the deployable program. The IDL JSON describes the program interface. The TypeScript file gives clients typed access to that IDL.

## Deploy to Gorbagana

Deploy all workspace programs to the provider cluster from `Anchor.toml`.

```bash
anchor deploy
```

You can also pass the provider cluster explicitly.

```bash
anchor deploy --provider.cluster https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Expected output includes a Program ID and transaction signature.

```txt
Program Id: PROGRAM_ID
Signature: TRANSACTION_SIGNATURE
```

Save both values. Your clients call the Program ID. The signature lets you inspect the deployment transaction.

<Callout type="info" title="Use native GOR for deployment">
  Anchor and Solana CLI output may say SOL or lamports. When the command targets Gorbagana RPC, the fee payer spends native GOR.
</Callout>

## Verify the deployment

Verify the deployed program before you wire clients to it.

Open the [Explorer](/network/explorer) and search for the deployment signature or Program ID. Check the transaction status, fee payer, logs, and program account.

Confirm the signature from the CLI.

```bash
solana confirm TRANSACTION_SIGNATURE -v \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Show program metadata.

```bash
solana program show PROGRAM_ID \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Expected output includes the Program ID, owner, ProgramData address, upgrade authority, last deployed slot, data length, and balance.

## Use the IDL

Use the local IDL from `target/idl` when you build frontend or script clients.

```txt
target/idl/hello_gorbagana.json
target/types/hello_gorbagana.ts
```

If your project publishes an on-chain IDL, fetch it after deployment.

```bash
anchor idl fetch -o target/idl/verified.json PROGRAM_ID
```

If the fetch fails, the program may not have a published IDL account. The local IDL is still useful for your own clients, but explorers and external integrators can only fetch an on-chain IDL if you publish one.

## Update a program

Update a deployed Anchor program while the current upgrade authority still controls it.

1. Change the program source.
2. Build the workspace.

   ```bash
   anchor build
   ```

3. Redeploy the workspace.

   ```bash
   anchor deploy
   ```

For a single program, use `anchor upgrade`.

```bash
anchor upgrade ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana.so \
  --program-id PROGRAM_ID \
  --provider.cluster https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Then verify the updated slot and data length.

```bash
solana program show PROGRAM_ID \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

## Manage authority

Anchor uses the same upgrade authority model as raw Solana CLI deployments.

Check the current authority.

```bash
solana program show PROGRAM_ID \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Transfer authority when another keypair should control future upgrades.

```bash
solana program set-upgrade-authority PROGRAM_ID \
  --new-upgrade-authority ./new-authority-keypair.json \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Make the program immutable only when you are sure it should never change again.

```bash
solana program set-upgrade-authority PROGRAM_ID \
  --final \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

<Callout type="warn" title="Immutable means permanent">
  After you remove upgrade authority, the program cannot be updated or closed.
</Callout>

## Common issues

<Accordions type="single">
<Accordion title="The deploy wallet has no native GOR">

Check the wallet Anchor uses.

```bash
DEPLOYER=$(solana address -k ~/.config/solana/id.json)
solana balance "$DEPLOYER" \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

Fund that wallet with native GOR before deploying. Program deployments need more funds than simple transfers because they allocate program data accounts.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Anchor is pointed at the wrong cluster">

Check the provider section in `Anchor.toml`.

```toml
[provider]
cluster = "https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf"
wallet = "~/.config/solana/id.json"
```

If you pass `--provider.cluster`, make sure the command-line value is also `https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf`.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="The Program ID does not match">

List keys and inspect the generated keypair.

```bash
anchor keys list
solana address -k ./target/deploy/hello_gorbagana-keypair.json
```

If the values differ from `declare_id!`, run:

```bash
anchor keys sync
anchor build
```

Then verify the Program ID before deploying again.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="The TypeScript IDL file is missing">

Run `anchor build` from the workspace root and check the output folders.

```bash
anchor build
ls target/idl
ls target/types
```

If you want the type file copied into your frontend, add a `[workspace]` `types` path in `Anchor.toml`.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="The IDL fetch fails">

Fetching only works when an IDL exists on-chain for that program.

```bash
anchor idl fetch -o target/idl/verified.json PROGRAM_ID
```

If this fails, use the local `target/idl/<program>.json` file for your own clients and publish an on-chain IDL only when your release process requires it.

</Accordion>

<Accordion title="The program cannot be upgraded">

Check program metadata.

```bash
solana program show PROGRAM_ID \
  --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

If the `Authority` field is missing, the program is immutable. If an authority is present, sign the upgrade with that authority.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>
